Technique: Chest radiography in AP projection.
Comparison: none.

Description:
Asymmetrical position.
Heterogeneous consolidation was seen in the apex and midfield of the right lung accompanied by pulling of the trachea, mediastinum and right border of the heart to the right.
A sheath was seen in the laterobasal right hemithorax covering the right costophrenic sinus, right hemidiaphragm, and part of the right border of the heart.
There was thickening of the apicollateral pleura of the right hemithorax.
Heart size is difficult to evaluate.
The aorta and superior mediastinum are difficult to evaluate.
The left hilum is thickened.
Fibroinfiltrates were seen throughout the left lung field, especially the apex and in the visualized right lung field.
Multiple ecstatic rings were also seen in the upper-middle field of the left lung accompanied by cavity formation in the middle field of the left lung.
The diaphragmatic arch and left costophrenic sinus were norm[REDACTED]
The bones that are visualized have an optimal impression of being intact.

Conclusion:
The picture is suggestive of duplex pulmonary tuberculosis with images of right lung atelectasis, DD/destroyed lung, accompanied by thickening of the right apicolateral pleura, right pleural effusion, bronchiectasis in the upper-middle field of the left lung and cavity formation in the middle field of the left lung
